subject: English
title: English 6 (PECTAA, SNC 2020)
questions: He was born in Makkah Mukarramah in the tribe of Quraish.
How old was Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) when his mother passed away?
His mother died when he was only six years old.
Who took care of him after his mother's death?
His grandfather Hazrat Abdul Muttalib took care of him.
At what age did he come under the guardianship of his uncle Abu Talib?
When he reached the age of eight his grandfather passed away and Abu Talib became his guardian.
Where did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) take Hazrat Khadija's caravan of goods?
Hazrat Khadija entrusted him to take her caravan of goods to Syria.
Who accompanied him on the trade journey and reported his honesty to Hazrat Khadija?
Her old and trusted slave Maysarah accompanied him and reported his integrity.
Even his enemies called him 'Al-Amin', which means:
He was called Al-Sadiq (the truthful) and Al-Amin (the trustworthy one).
To which emperor did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) write a letter inviting him to Islam?
He wrote to Heraclius, the Emperor of Byzantium.
Who did Heraclius question about the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Heraclius summoned Abu Sufyan, who admitted the Prophet's honesty and trustworthiness.
In the case of the woman from Bani Makhzum, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) taught us about:
He refused to excuse her crime due to her status, showing equal justice for all.
Eid-ul-Fitr marks the end of which month?
Eid-ul-Fitr commemorates the end of Ramadan and the start of Shawwal.
Shawwal is which month of the Islamic calendar?
The lesson calls Shawwal the 10th month in the Islamic calendar.
The night before Eid-ul-Fitr is known as:
After the Eid crescent is announced, the night is known as Chand Raat.
Obligatory payment to the poor before Eid prayer
Fitrana is an obligatory payment to the poor, given before Eid namaz.
Money or gifts children receive from elders on Eid is called:
Kids get 'Eidi' from elders as new currency notes or gifts.
What did Usman forget to bring for the kheer?
Mother said he forgot milk and rice, the main ingredients of kheer.
Who wrote 'The Lake Isle of Innisfree'?
The poem is by William Butler Yeats.
What does the poet want to build at Innisfree?
A small cabin of clay and wattles
'And a small cabin build there, of clay and wattles made.'
How many bean-rows will the poet have at Innisfree?
'Nine bean-rows will I have there, a hive for the honey-bee.'
What does the poet hear 'in the deep heart's core'?
Lake water lapping on the shore
He hears lake water lapping with low sounds by the shore, in the deep heart's core.
Where is the poet standing when he thinks of Innisfree?
On the roadway or on the pavements grey
'While I stand on the roadway, or on the pavements grey.'
The poet wants to go to Innisfree because he longs for:
a peaceful life close to nature
The poem contrasts the grey city with peaceful natural life at Innisfree.
Major Shabbir Sharif was awarded the:
He was awarded the Nishan-e-Haider, the highest military award.
When was Major Shabbir Sharif born?
He was born on April 28, 1943, in Kunjah, Gujrat.
Major Shabbir Sharif was the nephew of which Nishan-e-Haider holder?
He was the nephew of Nishan-e-Haider holder Major Raja Aziz Bhatti.
Which award did he receive on completing training at Pakistan Military Academy, Kakul?
He completed his training and was awarded the Sword of Honour.
In which war did Major Shabbir Sharif embrace martyrdom?
He fought in the 1971 Indo-Pakistani War in the Sulemanki Sector.
How old was Major Shabbir Sharif at the time of martyrdom?
At the time of martyrdom he was just 28 years old.
Major Shabbir Sharif is the only soldier to receive both the Nishan-e-Haider and the:
He is the only one to have received both Nishan-e-Haider and Sitara-e-Jurat.
Who moved in next door to Haziq and Ahmad?
They saw a family moving next door and welcomed them with dessert.
What did the mother first send to the new neighbours?
Mother gave them a bowl of dessert to take to the new neighbours.
What was the name of the boy who sat at the window?
His mother told them the boy's name was Jasim.
He had polio as a child
Jasim had polio at the age of two; his legs remained dysfunctional.
Why was Jasim afraid of school?
He was bullied by naughty boys in his previous school
He had a phobia of school because he had been bullied by naughty boys.
At first, what did Haziq and Ahmad think of Jasim?
Since he shut the window on seeing them, they thought him proud and rude.
The lesson in Unit 5 teaches us to:
treat special people with kindness and friendship
It teaches harmony: we should understand and befriend people with disabilities.
Why did Tina and her mother go shopping?
For a big party that night
They had a big party that night and needed things to cook a grand dinner.
What did Tina find on the way back from the market?
A woman collapsed on the road
They found a woman lying collapsed on the road.
Tina continued cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) until the ambulance came.
How many uninterrupted chest compressions did Tina give?
Why did Tina ask the crowd to move back?
So the lady could get fresh air
To clear the road for cars
She asked the crowd to move back so the lady could get fresh air.
According to the doctor, how many people know what to do in an emergency?
Only one in 20 people know what to do in an emergency.
CPR helps by providing oxygen-rich blood flow to the:
CPR keeps oxygen-rich blood flowing to the brain and other organs until treatment.
What kind of person was Mr. Shan, the newly appointed minister?
Mr. Shan was rude, offensive and a corrupt minister who never worked without bribery.
Why did the poor farmer come to Mr. Shan?
For approval of a water pump in his area
The farmer came for the approval of a water pump in his area.
What did Mr. Shan do when the farmer could not pay a bribe?
Tore up his application and had him thrown out
He rudely tore up the application and ordered his guards to throw the farmer out.
According to the Hadith quoted in the lesson, the curse of Allah is on:
both the briber and the recipient
'May the curse of Allah be on the briber and the recipient.'
Why did nobody stand up against Mr. Shan?
He had a strong wealthy background
Due to his strong wealthy background, nobody stood up against him.
Where were Danish and his grandfather lying on the hot summer night?
On the roof of their home
Danish was lying with his grandfather on the roof of their home.
According to Grandfather, why did they not need air conditioners in the past?
Many trees and green plots kept the temperature low
Many trees and green plots kept the temperature low.
What does 'overpopulation' mean, as explained in the lesson?
Too few people in a country
So large a population that people suffer as a result
Overpopulation is a situation where population is so large that people suffer as a result.
Why did people migrate from villages to cities, according to the lesson?
To get more opportunities and meet basic needs
People migrated to cities to get more and meet their basic needs.
The excessive use of coal, oil and fossil fuels is:
creating a negative impact on our planet
Excessive use of fossil fuels is creating a negative impact on the planet.
Why was the river near Grandfather's home no longer good for swimming?
It was polluted by human waste
They loved to swim in it, but it was now polluted by human waste.
Who was Mr. Akbar in the lesson?
A newly appointed teacher in the town
Mr. Akbar was a newly appointed teacher in the town.
Where did Mr. Akbar see Ameena reading?
He saw little Ameena sitting under the light pole reading an old book.
What was the hardest challenge Ameena faced in getting education?
One of the hardest challenges she encountered was poverty.
What did Ameena's father do for a living?
Her father was a scrap picker and could not bear her school expenses.
Where did Ameena get books to read?
She used to find old books from the scrap her father brought home.
What did Mr. Akbar promise the villagers?
Free teaching with books and stationery
He promised to teach without any fee, with books and stationery from school.
How did Ameena help the landlord?
She gave first aid for a snake bite
She tied his leg near the wound, washed it with soap and water and covered it with a clean dressing.
What did Ameena want to become?
She told the doctor she wanted to be a doctor.
Modern communication devices have made the world a:
Computers, mobile phones and electronic media have made the world a global village.
During the COVID-19 pandemic, what became a life saviour for many people?
Technology became a life saviour; people worked and studied from home.
How has technology helped in education, according to the lesson?
Students are facilitated with smart classes, multimedia, e-libraries and e-books.
Which are medical devices mentioned in the lesson?
X-rays, scan machines, operation devices and pacemakers help doctors and patients.
On which planet have scientists 'marked their presence'?
The lesson says they have marked their presence on Mars.
Which day is the poem in Unit 11 about?
The poem begins: 'Who knew that the day of 14th of August will tell the world...'
Who wrote the poem about 14th August in Unit 11?
The poem is by Dr. Tafazzal.
In the poem, Pakistan is called a home for a:
'A lovely land with sacred lands, and a home for a Musalman.'
'A Quaid's effort, a poet's dream' refers to:
Pakistan was the effort of Quaid-e-Azam and the dream of the poet Allama Iqbal.
Who is the founder of Pakistan?
Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah is the founder of Pakistan.
Why did Ms. Sara ask Basit to do his assignment again?
He could not complete it on time
Basit could not complete it; Zubair advised him to complete tasks on time.
What did Shiza and Tania learn about in their lesson?
That day they had a lesson about good citizenship.
What did Shiza and Tania do to improve their area?
Cleaned the street and planted trees
They cleaned their street and garden and planted new trees.
How long did it take the children to give their area a new look?
Within two hours a new look of their area emerged.
What did Shiza do when she saw strangers enter her neighbour's house?
Called the helpline and warned her neighbours
She called the helpline and told the neighbours to lock their inner door.
How did the strangers get into the house?
One climbed the wall and opened the gate
One of them climbed the wall and opened the gate for his friends.
keep surroundings clean and be vigilant
The teacher said a citizen must care for neighbours, keep surroundings clean and stay vigilant.
